title: Stream-of-Glitches Canvas — Sylvie scratchpad
content:
Context / intent:
This is a personal scratchpad for rapidly capturing odd output modes I keep hitting during late-night sampling. Not a polished report — more of a canvas to collect glitches, quick reproduce steps, ad-hoc rubric, and immediate hypotheses. Use as ephemeral working notes; if something looks important will lift into a ticket or weekly triage doc.

Short summary of current pain:
- Regression noticed between model:v2025-10-20 and model:v2025-11-12 where list-preservation degrades on longer enumerations (observed when prompt length > ~420 tokens).
- Occasional truncation of numeric suffixes ("1.", "2.") in outputs, replaced by bullets, causing downstream parsers to fail.
- Higher tendency to hallucinate tiny fictional citations when asked for brief legal summaries (we used to see far fewer hallucinated sources).

Quick reproduce seeds (do these first):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the following contract clause and list the obligations as numbered points:" + a ~450-token clause.
   - Expected: 4 numbered items, each preserved as "1.", "2.", etc.
   - Observed (v2025-11-12): items present but numbering lost or converted to "-" bullets for items 3..4.
   - Quick check: rerun with temperature=0.0 -> still converts numbering, so not stochastic-temp issue.

2) Prompt: "Extract the recipients and amounts from this payment schedule:" with a table of 6 rows.
   - Observed: rows 5-6 either merged or output as prose.

Ad-hoc micro-rubric (for quick triage):
Score 0-3 for each axis (0 worst, 3 best). Keep it very fast.
- Structural fidelity: preserves lists/tables and numbering exactly -> 0..3
- Hallucination rate (small falses like fake cites) -> 0..3 (0 many, 3 none)
- Concision: respects brief/long instruction -> 0..3
- Numeric exactness: preserves digits, suffixes, currency -> 0..3

Example quick snapshot (run: 2025-11-20, model:v2025-11-12):
- Test A (contract, 450 tokens): Structural fidelity=1, Hallucination=2, Concision=3, Numeric exactness=1
- Test B (payment table): Structural fidelity=0, Hallucination=3, Concision=2, Numeric exactness=1

Representative samples (paste raw outputs below for analyst use):
--- Prompt A (contract) ---
[redacted long clause pasted here in real runs]
Model output (verbatim):
1. Party A must provide funds within 30 days
2. Party B shall confirm receipt
- Party C must maintain insurance
- Ensure certificates are uploaded

Notes: numbering converted to bullets for last two items; parser downstream expects explicit numeric tokens, failed on extraction.

--- Prompt B (table) ---
Model output: "Payments will be made in stages. First, an initial sum will be sent. Subsequent payments follow based on milestones."
Notes: flattened table -> lost row boundaries.

Hypotheses (rapid):
- Tokenization/kernel change: a new kernel path for long-context attention introduces a subtle token boundary normalization that collapses period-after-digit into punctuation class that the LM emits as bullet.
- Post-processing filter: new formatting heuristic in post-process that tries to "clean" numbered lists when it sees repeated patterns and mistakenly normalizes.
- Training/regression: a micro-update to the small continuation dataset that included many bullet-only examples.

Quick tests to differentiate: (ranked by ease)
- Reproduce with temperature=0 and stream=false to rule out streaming join artifacts (done: still repro).
- Set decode options to force "preserve_newlines":true (if supported) or token-level constraints (disallow "-" at line start) -> if fixed, it's postprocess.
- Run model:v2025-10-20 (baseline) on exact same input to confirm delta (baseline preserves numbering).
- Inject explicit numbering tokens ("\n1\u241F") weird separator to see if model respects forced tokens; if yes, generator side, else serving side.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Add a small ticket with reproducer + both model ids + raw outputs + downstream parsing failure example (JIRA-ML-2143). I will attach the minimal failing input.
- Ask infra to cross-check kernel selection logs for inference requests that hit the failing path (time window: 2025-11-12 02:00-06:00 UTC) — maybe new binary rolled.
- Add a short unit test in samples-runner to flag when numbering is converted to bullets for N>3 lists.

Notes-to-self / heuristics I've tried:
- Doubling whitespace between items tends to help (hacky) — suggests model is sensitive to whitespace tokens.
- Forcing explicit markers like "(a)", "(b)" works but is not acceptable for customers.
- Shorter prompt (reduce clause to <300 tokens) removes the failure -> points to context-length-specific bug.

Other oddities I've logged (quick bullets):
- Tiny hallucinated citations: e.g., "see Section 4.2 of the 2019 Contract Law Guide" — not present in prompt. Mostly appears when asked for "brief legal summary" with default verbosity.
- Slightly higher false-positive entity extraction for organization names when sequence contains many numbers.

TODO (short):

- [ ] Grab kernel selection logs from infra (Devon)
